narrative:
There are two critical issues that are negatively impacting my finances caused by Summit Lending : # 1 PMI Removal - I have been unsuccessful in requesting the removal of my PMI. 
# 2 The monthly mortgage payment has fluctuated from {$2300.00} to a proposed {$2900.00}, with insufficient information about the rationale for this drastic increase.

PMI REMOVAL A PMI removal request was made via phone in XX/XX/XXXX. I was informed because of the amount of time I have owned the mortgage, I would likely be denied a 'desk removal ' of my PMI but would be offered the process to have my home appraised. I received a packet of information informing me of my option to request an appraisal late XXXX. 

This information details that an appraisal would be ordered within ten days. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I mailed a check for an appraisal and completed the PMI Removal Valuation form ( see attached ) and a check for {$320.00} for the cost of an appraisal. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, the check was cashed. 

Around XX/XX/XXXX, I called Summit Lending to check the status of my appraisal. I was informed that the appraisal was not ordered. The representative asked me if I had remodeled my home. I reiterated the information provided on the form mailed on XX/XX/XXXX. 

I asked when an appraisal would be ordered, but I was not provided an answer. 

I have called/emailed to follow up with Summit Lending on the following dates : XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX ( Director of Business Development XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX Each call ranged from 30-60 minutes ( roughly ). 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I was informed that an appraisal was requested. I was informed I would receive an appointment within seven days.

I have not received any call regarding an appointment for an appraisal.

ESCROW & MORTGAGE PAYMENT Around XX/XX/XXXX - I received a notification that my escrow was being adjusted, and thereby my mortgage payment would increase come XX/XX/XXXX. I called Summit Funding to understand this increase and learned that my escrow was incorrectly re-calculated and modified compared to what was calculated at closing. I closed on my home in XX/XX/XXXX. 

In the interim, I was requested by Summit Funding to pay an escrow deficit of {$6300.00}. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I authorized a payment to pay this deficit. I was informed by Summit Funding that my payments would increase to about {$2900.00}, even after this {$6300.00} payment to close the gap in escrow. I was told this new escrow spread was due to an increase in taxes. My escrow/impound amount is from {$520.00} to {$860.00} per month - an increase of {$340.00} or roughly a 35 % increase.

Please see the attached escrow analysis.

I have called my local county, XXXX, and they have indicated that they can not explain that increase. Their website indicates property taxes can only increase 2 % each year in the State of California based on inflation : hXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

As a result of Summit Fundings ' miscalculations in the past and this drastic increase, I have requested a detailed breakdown of the analysis that I was told would be received today.

IN SUM My mortgage payments continue to increase, and Summit Funding continues to demand payments for services not rendered and an escrow spread without rationale. This is severely impacting my ability to plan, per the agreement when this mortgage was closed.

This assistance of the Consumer Financial Protection Agency is greatly appreciated.

narrative: On XX/XX/XXXX I purchased furniture from XXXX XXXX XXXX  in XXXX, UT. I used a Discover credit card to make the {$5500.00} purchase. The furniture was to be delivered later due to supply chain issues. I received monthly updates from the furniture company telling me delivery was being further delayed and that they were working to get furniture to me as fast as they could. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received the last email update. On XX/XX/XXXX the furniture store employee who had sold us the furniture informed us that due to financial problems of the company we would not be getting the furniture. I immediately ( on XX/XX/XXXX ) disputed the {$5500.00} charge with Discover. I also tried to contact the owner of the furniture store but was not successful. Discover initially gave me the {$5500.00} credit to my card while they did an investigation. After the investigation, Discover informed me they reversed my {$5500.00} credit because they found it to be a valid charge. The only documentation Discover sent me relating to the investigation was a copy of the credit card charge I made with the furniture company ( this was the charge I was disputing so this was not any meaningful documentation ). The company is out of business and has been issued a citation by state division of consumer protection. The division has been unable to contact the owner directly. I have contacted and discussed my dispute with Discover dispute representatives at least five times since my dispute was denied. I was told each tme that to get credit for the {$5500.00} charge, I would need a letter from the furniture ompany owner on company letterhead indicating that my furniture was not delivered and that I was due a refund from the company. This is impossible because the owner is no where to be found and will not respond to any form of communication. On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent a letter to Discover containing a link to and excerpts from the Fair Credit Billing Act Sec.1666 Correction of Billing Errors '' that indicates that if I ( obligor ) make a timely dispute ( to the creditor ) of the charge, indicating that I did not receive goods for which I was charged ( which I did- I made the dispute on the day I learned I would not ever receive the furniture ) then, before being able to deny the dispute, the credit card company is required to investigate and determine that the goods were actually delivered and then provide me ( the obligor ) with a statement of the determination [ Sec . 1666 ( a ) ( 3 ) ( B ) ( ii ) ]. Discover did no such investigation and did not provide me such a statement.

product_raw: Credit card or prepaid card
narrative: I pay my credit card bill each month to avoid the 19.99 % interest charge. Last month, while paying my bill on the Citi bank website, a pop up offered a {$20000.00} flex plan loan with an 8.99 % interest rate. I took the loan to help pay for my sons post education. I received my bill and paid the balance of my purchases for the month plus the plan payment amount for the Citi flex loan. I received my next bill and there is {$98.00} in additional interest not related to the loan. I call Citi. Thirty-two minutes later, the Citi rep confirms that although the loan plan payment amount is itemized separate on the bill, the application of the payment results in being charged the higher 19.99 % interest rate on the purchases. In other words, the 8.99 % loan results in being charged 19.99 % on the purchases UNLESS the bill is paid in full ( both the loan and the purchase balance is paid in full ). Which means that while the loan balance is technically 8.99 %, youre payment is being applied in a way which results in an overall blended rate that is much higher. The only way to only to use the loan as sold, is to take the loan and NEVER use the card again until the loan is paid off. This is all very confusing, but certainly unethical. I asked for an email to complain. She said there was only a PO address. I can not believe this is legal and being pushed on consumers. Im educated, worked XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, and I am sure many others who carry balances are being hoodwinked into increasing their debt at interest rates while beyond what was sold to them. She mentioned fine print. I honestly dont recall anything more than clicking accept, but even if I did, there is no way this is being explained in a way which is ethical.

product: Mortgage
product_raw: Mortgage
narrative:
We had an FHA mortgage with Rocket Mortgage for our home that we purchased in XX/XX/XXXX, which we recently sold. We built a new home and were scheduled to close on the sale of the old home on XX/XX/XXXX, but due to delays with the buyers lender, the buyers were unable to close until XX/XX/XXXX. The mortgage payoff amount that had been quoted to the title company was supposedly good through XX/XX/XXXX. Our title agency wired the proceeds from the sale to Rocket Mortgage, and they included extra funds per down to account for any extra interest that may have been accrued. 

Rocket mortgage received the transfer on XXXX, and left me a voicemail saying it was short and they needed to collect the additional funds. I didnt not listen to this voicemail until XXXX ( sometimes my phone does not show me I have voicemails until days later ), and I immediately called them. Rocket Mortgage stated that because I did not respond for 2 days, they rejected the wire transfer and that they would have to generate a new payoff amount for me. I contacted our title company, and they were SHOCKED, because they said normally a mortgage lender would reach out to the title company directly about a shortage. Further, they stated they sent more than the payoff amount requested, to account for any extra interest due to delays with the closing process. 

I left a voicemail for the person who was designated as our contact person at Rocket. She called me back and stated it is their policy that they call the consumer, not the title company, and they collect the extra funds from the consumer. The funds were supposedly rejected yesterday, but the title company has not received the funds from the transfer back. Meanwhile, interest keeps accruing on this mortgage that we still hold, on a house we no longer own. The title agent said that she has never heard of a lender doing things this way, and that it seems like they are trying to take advantage of people. I have already spent hours on the phone trying to resolve something that should not even have been an issue. I do not want other people to have to go through this, especially those that may just accept what Rocket is telling them at face value and hand over the cash.

XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Reported late payments to credit companies against consumer law 15 U.S. Code 1681a - Definitions ; rules of construction ( 2 ) Exclusions.Except as provided in paragraph ( 3 ), the term consumer report does not include ( A ) subject to section 1681s3 of this title, any ( i ) report containing information solely as to transactions or experiences between the consumer and the person making the report ; ( ii ) communication of that information among persons related by common ownership or affiliated by corporate control ; 15 U.S. Code 1666b - Timing of payments ( a ) Time to make payments A creditor may not treat a payment on a credit card account under an open end consumer credit plan as late for any purpose, unless the creditor has adopted reasonable procedures designed to ensure that each periodic statement including the information required by section 1637 ( b ) of this title is mailed or delivered to the consumer not later than 21 days before the payment due date.

( b ) Grace period If an open end consumer credit plan provides a time period within which an obligor may repay any portion of the credit extended without incurring an additional finance charge, such additional finance charge may not be imposed with respect to such portion of the credit extended for the billing cycle of which such period is a part, unless a statement which includes the amount upon which the finance charge for the period is based was mailed or delivered to the consumer not later than 21 days before the date specified in the statement by which payment must be made in order to avoid imposition of that finance charge. 

15 U.S. Code 1605 - Determination of finance charge ( a ) Finance charge defined Except as otherwise provided in this section, the amount of the finance charge in connection with any consumer credit transaction shall be determined as the sum of all charges, payable directly or indirectly by the person to whom the credit is extended, and imposed directly or indirectly by the creditor as an incident to the extension of credit. The finance charge does not include charges of a type payable in a comparable cash transaction. The finance charge shall not include fees and amounts imposed by third party closing agents ( including settlement agents, attorneys, and escrow and title companies ) if the creditor does not require the imposition of the charges or the services provided and does not retain the charges. Examples of charges which are included in the finance charge include any of the following types of charges which are applicable : ( 1 ) Interest, time price differential, and any amount payable under a point, discount, or other system or additional charges.

( 2 ) Service or carrying charge.

( 3 ) Loan fee, finders fee, or similar charge.

( 4 ) Fee for an investigation or credit report.

( 5 ) Premium or other charge for any guarantee or insurance protecting the creditor against the obligors default or other credit loss.

( 6 ) Borrower-paid mortgage broker fees, including fees paid directly to the broker or the lender ( for delivery to the broker ) whether such fees are paid in cash or financed.

The sales rep advised us that making the switch with XXXX was fairly easy but we had to make sure MTH was aware and could update the lot number and address on our loan. narrative:
The company is PayPal and the application causing the problem ( for me ) is Venmo. As you may be aware the IRS change the the reporting rules for companies involved in Person to Person Payments such as Venmo, PayPal, XXXX XXXX, etc. As a result if a customer of XXXX of these companies receives a payment for " good and services '' and those payments ( for goods and services ) within the same calendar year have a cumulative total of {$600.00} or more, the Company ( in this case Venmo ) is required to report that total amount to the IRS and issue the customer a XXXX. 

This situation is I have XXXX transactions on my account where friends of mine were paying me back for money they borrowed from me ( as I paid the entire bill for the event or function we attended together ) and they mistakenly mark the payments on Venmo for " good and services '' vs " friends and family ''. As you may know, the receiver of funds on Venmo ( in this case me ) has no control over how a sender marks or codes a payment and is not able to see it until it hits the account. The only way they know it was marked ( in this case inaccurately ) is when the transaction has hit the account because Venmo charges the receiver a fee for payments they receive for goods and services. 

I had XXXX payments from friends that were sent to me in XXXX where my friends mistakenly marked those payments for good and services and I noticed it when I saw the net payment amount was lower than what they owed me as a result of the transaction fee Venmo charges for payments for goods and services ( there is not transaction fee charged for payments to friends and family ). The XXXX payments in question are : XXXX from - XXXX for {$1600.00} on XX/XX/XXXX XXXX from - XXXX. for {$500.00} on XX/XX/XXXX XXXX from - XXXX. for {$1300.00} on XX/XX/XXXX Venmo reversed the transaction fee charged on these payments for goods and services because after they reviewed them and with speaking to me and in XXXX case ( XXXX ) they realized the payments were marked in error by the sender and the payments should have been marked friends and family. However, they will not adjust their system to move these payments that were marked in error to the correct category and now they are going to knowing report in error to the IRS the cumulative total of these payments {$3400.00} and issue me a XXXX. You can imagine the problems this is going to cause. I do not sell good or services on line or to anyone else. I do not have a company that does either. This is essentially my money that I've already paid taxes on being given back to me by a friend because I paid the entire bill in total as a convenience to the group ( I essentially loaned the money to them ) and they paid me back. 

My complaint is as follows : -Payments sent to me automatically hit my account without any approval from me. Therefore, I have no way of knowing if the sender mistakenly codes them incorrectly until after they have hit the account. If a mistake like this is made it's 100 % out of my control. 

XXXXVenmo recognized the payment was mistakenly coded as for goods and services and refunded the transaction fee they charge for payments for goods and services. Therefore they know it's a mistake as well. 

-Even though they have acknowledged the payments were not coded accurately ( by refunding the transaction fee ) they are going to still report the cumulative total of those payments to the IRS XXXX as payments received for goods and services. 

I believe XXXX things should happen. First and foremost if Venmo acknowledged the payments were coded incorrectly as payments for goods and services ( by their actions of refunding the transaction fee ) then they should adjust those payments in their system as well and not knowingly report inaccurate data ( the total of these payments ) to the IRS. By issuing me a XXXX with inaccurate data, it is going to cost me time, money, and grief in working with the IRS to resolve this issue. 

Secondly, the system at Venmo should have some sort of confirmation process where the receiver of a payment can verify the accuracy all payments before those payments hit their account. If Venmo has made the decision to not recode payments once they hit a customers account, regardless of the accuracy of how those payments are covered then they need to create a process so the consumer can protect themselves from potentially have a mess on their hands with their taxes and the IRS. 

I have spoken to the representatives at Venmo multiple times and they are staying they can not adjust these payments that were coded incorrectly by the sender, even-though they acknowledged they are not accurate ( by refunding the transaction fee they charge on payments for good and services ) and they will send that inaccurate reporting to the IRS and XXXX me an inaccurate XXXX as well. I know they can make the adjustment on the coding of the payment to correct it, but they are choosing not to. Why Venmo is knowingly sending inaccurate data to the IRS that is negatively impacting their customers is alarming to me and I would think it would be alarming to the CFPB as well.

We were given a HELOC back in I think 2016 with Susquehanna, then BB & T, and now Truist Bank. We were told at that time that the way the line worked is we could take out an amount and choose either a fixed rate option where the rate would be fixed and we would pay back a certain amount of pricipal and interest over a certain number of years or we could just use it more like a regular credit line where we could take out an amount and the interest rate could adjust. We initially after receiving the line, too out I think about {$35000.00} and fixed that rate at about 3.75 %. Over the years we have taken out and pay back smaller amounts at the adjustable rate option. As of this past XXXX we did not have any amount owe other than the fixed rate. Any time we used the adjustable rate option wehad paid it back quickly. 

I went into the branch on XXXX XXXX this past XXXX, because we had some projects coming up and I knew rates were on the rise, so I wanted to see about taking out an additional $ XXXX {$15000.00} and choosing the fixed rate option. The rate I was quote was XXXX?? %. I know it was under 5 %. Since that rate was still so good, I chose to take out {$15000.00} and fix the rate/payment. When the bills arrived, I paid the amount due for the first several months. Everything seemed good. 

This past Fall, I started getting noticed about past due amounts, late fees, and rate changes. I called the number on the statement and was told they could not help me and I had to call the branch. I called the branch several times in XXXX and each time was told that the person had to speak to a supervisor, would get back to me etc. They never got back to me and eventually told me that the manager I had worked with to take out the additional {$150000.00} was no longer there. I asked for them to send me the paperwork on the loan and was told they could not find it. I paid the amount I believed was due. The bills arriving in the mail were super unclear on what was actually owed and kept referring to interest rate changes, which should not be because I had chosen a fixed rate option. Today I tried again to call the main number since the branch was no help. The person I spoke with found my line of credit and the original fixed rate portion but could not find anywhere that said anything about the {$15000.00} I took out OR the rate being adjustable or anything at all about. She could not tell me what I owed or what had been messed up concerning fixing the rate. She told me I had to wait 48 business hours to hear from a manager. 
However, at this point this is the fourth time I have been told to wait a few days to speak with a manager and I am very concerned that I am being charged a higher rate than I agreed to, that I don't know the amount to pay, that I am being charged late fees, and I am concerned that this will negatively affect my credit.

narrative:
I'm a recently retired XXXX XXXXXXXX after 24 years with one employer. I received a large payment from my company 's retirement account. While I was trying to determine how to invest these funds, I decided to open a Citibank high yield savings account so that these funds could earn interest while I worked on my investment strategy. I opened the Citibank account on XX/XX/23 and funded it with an electronic transfer from my checking account with XXXX XXXX XXXX. I made two additional deposits on XX/XX/23 and XX/XX/23. My total deposits into the Citibank high yield savings account were {$220000.00}. 
After meeting with my investment advisor, we determined the best use for the funds. As such, I started moving funds back to my XXXX XXXX XXXX  checking account from the Citibank high yield savings account. I was able to move {$15000.00} by XX/XX/23. Then, on XX/XX/23, I received an email from Citibank informing me that my high yield savings account would close within 60 days due to a violation to the terms of my agreement. The message provided a phone number to call to get more information. I spent countless hours discussing the issue with Citi customer service. I was transferred numerous times to various teams, but nobody could tell me anything additional other than what the email contained. I asked on several occasions to speak with management. I was told each time that they were all in meetings and not available. One individual told me he would have a manager call me. That didn't happen. I was also hung up on during one call. I simply wanted an explanation as to what I did as I felt there had to be a misunderstanding by Citibank. I was never able to talk to someone that could help. 
Now, it's been several weeks and I haven't received any additional communications, nor do I have access to my funds. My online access has been blocked for all my Citibank products, including a credit card I've held for a decade. I would like someone to discuss the situation with me and provide an explanation for what happened, and more importantly at this point, send me my {$200000.00} in retirement funds. Each day that passes, I lose significant interest income and any upside I would have from the investment opportunities I identified with my financial advisor. I don't understand how Citibank can permit a large transfer of money into an account but not allow those funds to flow out when needed. This is a significant amount of money for my retirement that Citi is holding hostage while treating me like a criminal.

Despite requests sent in writing via US Postal Service in XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX has failed to supply a contract to which they are a party nor any other evidence to support the claim that this account is valid. They are in violation of the FCRA, TILA, and the Gramm-Leech-Biley Act Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), a consumer reporting agency is only allowed to furnish information about a consumer 's credit history with the consumer 's consent. Specifically, Section 604 of the FCRA states that a consumer reporting agency may only furnish a consumer 's credit report to those who have a " legitimate business need for the information '' and who certify that the information will be used for " permissible purposes. '' Section 604 also requires that the consumer be notified in writing of the request for the credit report and that the consumer has the right to know the nature and scope of the request. 

Furthermore, Section 607 of the FCRA requires that a consumer reporting agency maintain reasonable procedures to ensure that the information they report is accurate. If a consumer disputes the accuracy of any information on their credit report, the consumer reporting agency must investigate the dispute and correct any inaccuracies. 

Under Section 605B of the FCRA, a victim of identity theft can request that the credit reporting agencies block any information that is the result of fraudulent activity. Specifically, Section 605B ( a ) ( 1 ) states : " A consumer may notify a consumer reporting agency that the consumer disputes the accuracy of information in a consumer report on the consumer on the grounds that the information relates to a fraudulent transaction or to an account or to other products or services that were obtained as a result of identity theft. '' This includes items that were created by an imposter, or those that were created by the thief using my personal information. 

Furthermore, under Section 621 ( a ) ( 2 ) ( A ) of the FCRA, I have the right to submit a sworn affidavit to the credit reporting agencies stating that the information on my credit report is the result of identity theft. The affidavit should include a statement that I did not create the accounts or authorize the charges and that I am not responsible for them. I have attached a copy of the FTC 's Identity Theft Affidavit to this letter. 

In light of these laws, I respectfully request that any and all items on my credit report that are the result of identity theft be removed immediately. I did not consent to the reporting of fraudulent charges or accounts and therefore, they should be removed in accordance with Section 604 of the FCRA.

narrative:
XXXX - took out a primary loan as well as a " soft second '' with Bank of America to purchase a primary/only residence Between XXXX and XXXX mortgage payments became difficult to impossible to make due to difficulties with the mother of my children. My options were either leave myself or evict my children and their mother. I could not afford rent as well as the mortgage nor could I evict my own children. 

XXXX - struggled to make payments on the " soft second '' ( as well as the primary ) XXXX - made a payment " soft second '' after missing several payments XXXX - Bank of America " charged off '' the " soft second '' loan XXXX - the last tax document issued with respect to the " soft second '' was submitted to the IRS was for the XXXX tax year Prior to foreclosure, the primary loan changed servicers to " XXXX '', who did get in contact with me regarding foreclosure mitigation. 
No contact was made regarding the soft second, which I was unaware was charged off. At the time, I thought that loan was lumped in with the primary loan re : who was servicing the loan and handling the eventual foreclosure. I had no reason to think otherwise, given the situation and that both loans originated with the same company. 

XXXX - foreclosure XXXX XX/XX/XXXX - foreclosure complete, with the transaction amount being over {$2000.00} more than the amount owed on the primary loan and about {$10000.00} less than the market value noted on the 1099-A. 
There is no record of any of the excess being applied to the " soft second '' loan, which had been charged off two years prior.

2023 January- the charged off " soft second '' changes servicers from Bank of America itself to Capital Management Services I was not notified of this change. In addition to not notifying me of this change, Bank of America gave the new servicer a contact address that I have no association with ( the address is for a strip mall in a town where I have never lived ) despite Bank of America having sent correspondence to where I lived in XXXX, which is in the same building where I currently reside ( just across the hall from the last address -- it is a 3-unit home ). 

Right around this time, I was in the process of trying to secure a pre-approval for a loan to purchase a home with my wife ( in no small part as means to improve my children 's custody situation ). We went through " hard '' credit checks, and so on. 
Because of debt on my wife 's side of things, we have to pause our search to improve our DTI ratio and the issue with my loan remains hidden. 

XXXX - I still am unaware of the change in services for the " soft second '' ( or that it still exists as I thought it went with the foreclosure ). The discrepancies are found when we go to apply for pre-approval after improving the DTI ratio and my wife receiving a promotion. 
Traversing the Bank of America phone system to try to find out what happened to this secondary loan is almost impossible because the account number is not recognized by their phone system nor is my SSN. 
Bank of America Collections has some record of the account, but only that it has been sent to a new servicer. They seem certain that it was some kind of loan taken out for home repairs or the like as they can not figure out why I would think that it would be associated with the foreclosure, even though it was taken out to purchase the home along with another Bank of America loan. 
When asked for the note, etc., associate with the loans as well as a copy of the agreement ( s ) sign, they are unable/unwilling to provide any information. They say they will send the payment history. They told me that the collections had been sent to an outside servicer and provided the number. 
I called the new servicer and found that Bank of America had provided them with the incorrect address. I requested the send me information regarding this debt. I received a notice/bill, but no information regarding how the service was transferred, etc. I have subsequently requested any and all information they may have on this debt. 

Somewhere in all of this, Bank of America neglected to ethically handle the " soft second '' both by charging it off without notice, despite a recent payment, as well as not applying any excess in the sale to the second mortgage and not getting fair market value for the house to absolve the majority of the soft second along with the primary loan. They also neglected to provide the new servicers information to me and provided that servicer an incorrect address such that I was unaware that the debt had changed hands.

product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
product_raw: Credit reporting, credit repair services, or other personal consumer reports
narrative:
As a victim of fraudulent activity related to an opened car loan that I did not authorize, I am very concerned about the impact this has had on my financial wellbeing. According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), I have the right to dispute any fraudulent information on my credit report and seek restitution for any damages caused by the fraud.

Under FCRA section 1681g, I am entitled to receive a copy of my credit report from all three major credit bureaus and review it for accuracy. If I find any inaccuracies, I have the right to dispute them with the credit bureau and the creditor that provided the information. Additionally, under FCRA section 1681e, creditors and credit bureaus have a duty to ensure that the information they report is accurate and up-to-date. In this case, the car loan that was fraudulently opened in my name should not have been reported to the credit bureaus without my consent, and any negative impacts to my credit score resulting from this fraudulent activity should be rectified.

Furthermore, under TILA section 1641, if the creditor sells or assigns the car loan to another party, they are required to notify me in writing of the transfer within 30 days. If the creditor fails to provide this notification, I have the right to rescind the loan for up to three years after the loan is made. Given that I did not authorize the opening of this car loan, it is unlikely that I received the required notification of transfer, which may give me further grounds to challenge the legitimacy of the loan.

As a victim of fraud, I should not be held liable for any debts incurred without my knowledge or consent. According to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), debt collectors are prohibited from engaging in any abusive, deceptive, or unfair practices in attempting to collect a debt. This includes attempting to collect a debt that is not owed or attempting to collect an inflated amount. If the car loan in question was fraudulently opened and I did not benefit from the proceeds of the loan, I should not be held responsible for repayment of the loan or any associated fees or interest.

In light of these laws and protections, I urge the creditor and any collection agencies involved in this matter to take swift action to rectify this situation. I should have a provisional credit added to my account for the full amount of the fraudulent loan, and any negative impacts to my credit score resulting from this fraudulent activity should be removed. I also request that the creditor and any collection agencies cease all attempts to collect on this debt until the matter is resolved and I am provided with sufficient evidence that the debt is valid and owed by me.

Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I look forward to a swift and satisfactory resolution to this issue.

It's quite another to send someone a picture of your driver 's license.

All you get are copied and pasted responses. 

Also - the website says that I should check my email for more information regarding the account suspension. The lady I spoke with said the same thing. But I never received an email from Venmo telling me the account was suspended. I didn't get any communication from them at all until I reached out. ( And, yes, I checked my spam folder. ) They told me in writing that I had a verified bank account that I could transfer funds in to and now they won't let me access those funds. And they are asking for extremely sensitive personal information. 

I noticed that Paypal ( who owns Venmo ) settled a lawsuit with them in XXXX due to privacy violations and lack of transparency with their users. Guess that lawsuit didn't teach Venmo anything.

narrative: Someone fraudulently opened an Ally Bank " Everyday Cash Back '' MasterCard using my credit information and under my name and social security number. When I received the notification that I had been approved for the Ally credit card ( that I absolutely did not apply for ) I immediately called Ally 's fraud and security department to report this fraudulent activity. I was tossed from one customer service representative to another without any real explanations why. Each representative asked for my full social security number, and when I told them I was nervous about giving it to them because obviously my SSN had already been compromised, they told me that was the only way to confirm my identity. When I finally reached someone in the security department that said they could help me, this costumer service representation told me she could " lock '' the account so it can't be accessed, but she couldn't close the account because it had been opened too recently ( the same day as my call ) and still needed to be processed. They asked me to call back the next day to fully close the fraudulent account. When I called back the next day, the lady I spoke with said they would need to do an investigation before fully closing the account. This is not what I was told the day before. Then I was told I needed to wait 7-10 business days for documents they would be sending me in the mail to fill out and then send back, in order to " get more information for the investigation ''. So I'm supposed to sit here and take their word that my account has been locked and the perpetrator can't access those funds? There is no way for me to actually know that someone hasn't already spent the whole limit of the credit card by now. They could have maxed out the card and I would have no idea. This has been a very stressful situation and I've tried getting it under control as fast as I possibly can, but Ally has not been helpful in the least bit. No one seemed to know exactly how to handle this or what to tell me. This can't be the first time someone has had their identity stolen and was used to get an Ally credit card. So why isn't there an immediate action SOP in place for situations like this? Altogether, Ally was not an easy or helpful company to deal with this incredibly stressful and harmful situation.

narrative:
On XX/XX/2024, at XXXXXXXX XXXX  I prepared to transfer my money from my XXXX checking to my savings account with Marcus, as I had just been paid according to my recent transactions. I had about {$710.00} in my Marcus savings prior. 

When I tried to log in through the Marcus app, the screen displayed that I needed to log out, and it automatically logged me out, not even a few seconds later. I was surprised but didn't think much of it since the app had a face ID login, and I tried to log back in like normal. When I put in my information on the username and password, the screen showed me that the username was not found. I tried logging in until a screen displayed a phone number to call and a text saying, " We've temporarily locked your account. Please call us to have it unlocked, '' which I did first thing in the morning. 

The person on the phone asked for my information, and I gave my personal information, to which they responded, " Please call us again when you have the correct information. '' I was shocked as I had emails and phone text messages from my Marcus account with the same personal information I had given them. I called again the next day, and this time, they asked for my secret code, which I still needed to remember as the automatic face ID login assured me I didn't need to manually memorize my information as they have a secure login system. 

I called repeatedly and still need help to unlock my account. I was told, " Please call us again when you have the correct information. " I gave up as I realized I had made a mistake in not manually memorizing my secret code. I also manually tried to reset my username and password through the app, which didn't work either. 

I didn't know what else to do but was puzzled when I still received emails from Marcus about my account. Then, I learned about CFPB from my manager, which is why I am writing this complaint. If Marcus recognizes my email and a savings account clearly tied to my person, why can't I log in and have access to my money? Could you let me know why I am not given any other way to prove I am the owner of my own account?

12 CFR 1016.1 Purpose and scope. 
( a ) Purpose. This part governs the treatment of nonpublic personal information about consumers by the financial institutions listed in paragraph ( b ) of this section. This part : ( 1 ) Requires a financial institution to provide notice to customers about its privacy policies and practices ; ( 2 ) Describes the conditions under which a financial institution may disclose nonpublic personal information about consumers to nonaffiliated third parties ; and ( 3 ) Provides a method for consumers to prevent a financial institution from disclosing that information to most nonaffiliated third parties by opting out of that disclosure, subject to the exceptions in 1016.13, 1016.14, and 1016.15. 12 CFR 1016.4 Initial privacy notice to consumers required.

( a ) Initial notice requirement. You must provide a clear and conspicuous notice that accurately reflects your privacy policies and practices to : ( 1 ) Customer. An individual who becomes your customer, not later than when you establish a customer relationship, except as provided in paragraph ( e ) of this section; and ( 2 ) Consumer. A consumer, before you disclose any nonpublic personal information about the consumer to any nonaffiliated third party, 12 CFR 1016.7 Form of opt out notice to consumers ; opt out methods.

Section ( a ) ( 1 ) Form of opt out notice.

If you are required to provide an opt out notice under 1016.10 ( a ), you must provide a clear and conspicuous notice to each of your consumers that accurately explains the right to opt out under that section. The notice must state : ( i ) That you disclose or reserve the right to disclose nonpublic personal information about your consumer to a nonaffiliated third party ; ( ii ) That the consumer has the right to opt out of that disclosure; and ( iii ) A reasonable means by which the consumer may exercise the opt out right.

When determining whats reasonable and fair, we should focus on the issue of liability ; common queries include, but are not limited to, the following ( i ) whether Cash2Bitcoin did not take notice of any rule, law, or regulation, and/or possibly missed any material elements of the relevant bylaws or codes of conduct, that may have prevented them from protecting my financial safety ; ( ii ) whether by virtue of Cash2Bitcoins custodianship over my funds or by its control over them, they owed a fiduciary duty to the me and if so, whether that duty was breached ; ( iii ) whether Cash2Bitcoin promoted the transaction ( s ) in question despite being aware of the nature of the transaction ( s ) in question ( iv ) whether Cash2Bitcoin was in compliance with its own policies and procedures ; ( v ) whether Cash2Bitcoin owed duties to myself, what the scope of those duties was, and whether Cash2Bitcoin did not uphold those duties ; ( vi ) whether Cash2Bitcoins conduct was unfair ; and ( vii ) whether Cash2Bitcoin has within its power the ability to, and should, compensate me for the harm that has befallen me.

Upon identification of such unusual or suspicious activity, it is crucial that the relevant staff member adequately describe the factors making an activity or transaction suspicious, thoroughly depict the extent and nature of this activity, and properly communicate to the customer that such activity meets the relevant criteria of fraud.

In providing its services to a customer, a financial institution is legally required to exercise the care and skill of a diligent, prudent banker. In this case, the payment service provider should not turn a blind eye to known facts pointing to a real possibility that their customer is being scammed. In other words, Cash2Bitcoin must have had special knowledge of what was occurring or been alerted to a real possibility of fraud taking place. The financial institution must have known or reasonably ought to have known that I was dealing with a scammer.

Granted, there is room for diversity of view insofar as reasonableness is concerned. Indeed, there is a sense in which the standard of care of the reasonable person involves in its application a subjective element.

However, it must be remembered that the correct test is always reasonable care in all circumstances, not average care. The fact that most people behave in a certain way may be good evidence that the conduct is reasonable, but this is not necessarily the case. Although reasonableness is a very fluid concept, all of the evidence suggests that Cash2Bitcoin did not foresee the fraud and disregarded even the most obvious dangers in this respect.

Situations do tend to repeat themselves and it is advisable to examine previous outcomes to see how the standard of the reasonable person should be applied, and that lessons can be learned from the errors of the past.

Apropos of the fluidity of the concept of reasonableness, all Cash2Bitcoin has done in this regard is set up a dichotomy of having or not having the legal obligation under consideration, however, that does not go one-inch toward explaining why various regulatory authorities, have maintained that financial institutions can, and should, protect consumers using their systems, advanced technologies, and rich experience.

Now it is 40 days away from the sale of my house NO ONE has reached out to talk to me about the trial payments no emails have been returned. I have requested for several managers and even spoke with one who stated she would reach out to underwriting and they have not returned my call from two weeks ago. Now they have reversed my funds that I have paid and can not or will not tell me what is going on. It takes them weeks to months to send documents and they are not allowing me sufficient time to collect my documents and get to sent in, for example on the date they sent the approval letter it was never actually mailed to me it was placed in a hidden spot on my online account and because I am on modification my online account has certain features limited. I have sent in another modification packet on yesterday just because my sale date is close and I havent heard back from them. Basically Freedom mortgage has said Im being penalized for making payments early however the agreement I had with them was to make trial payments in a timely manner and all payments have been made yet they are not attempting to honor the agreement.

The complainant never intended to grant legal title in any of her property to any of the parties previously mentioned, including Mr. Cooper Group. 
The Purchase Money Security Deed was solely intended to secure the complainants repayment of the mortgage, which she tendered on XX/XX/XXXX. The complainant also served a Revocation of Power of Attorney and Security Interest to the defendants on XX/XX/XXXX, which stripped them of their Power of Attorney and agent-in fact authorities and removed their right to a Power of Sale of the real property of subject.

The complainant obtained a Forensic Mortgage Securitization Audit which provided XXXX XXXX data proving that not only was her mortgage account already settled and repaid to Mr. Cooper Group, but that Mr. Cooper Group has converted and securitized the complainants mortgage chattels and are currently trading them on stock exchange markets and retaining all the profits. The complainant received a copy of the promissory note with the allonge from the debt collector XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, and the note does not contain a special indorsement signifying the assignment of the mortgage from XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. narrative:
1. Inflated Appraisal by XXXX, XXXX Rocket Mortgage appointed XXXX, XXXX, to conduct the appraisal for my mortgage. I have substantial evidence to suggest that the property appraisal was deliberately inflated to justify a higher loan amount. This practice of inflating appraisals is a form of mortgage fraud that directly impacts the borrower by increasing the loan-to-value ratio, which can lead to financial instability and a higher likelihood of default. This is also a violation of federal law RESPA ( see Violations and Codes on last page ). 

2. Conflict of Interest and Deceptive Practices by Realtor My realtor, XXXX XXXX, was appointed by Rocket Mortgage and acted in the interest of Rocket Mortgage rather than in my best interest as her client. When I expressed concerns about the loan officer, XXXX XXXX, and the sudden increase in my approved loan amount from {$410000.00} to {$420000.00} ( despite higher taxes on the second property ), XXXX XXXX attempted to convince me that my concerns were unfounded and " all in my head. '' She frequently communicated with XXXX XXXX privately about my concerns and would subsequently try to persuade me to proceed with the transaction, regardless of the red flags I raised. Because of this, I felt pressured to sign closing documents because I thought I would be legally responsible for this property. 

3. Bait-and-Switch Tactics Rocket Mortgage engaged in bait-and-switch tactics by initially offering favorable loan terms, only to alter them during the closing process. When I questioned these changes and attempted to seek advice from other mortgage lenders, XXXX XXXX, my loan officer responded clearly with an attitude stating, " I did not know other companies were involved, '' which I interpreted as an attempt to shame me for seeking alternative advice and being knowledgeable about my options. 

4. Approval for a Loan Beyond My Means I was initially pre-approved for a loan amount of {$410000.00}, which was suddenly increased to {$420000.00} without a proper reassessment of my ability to repay. This practice, known as " loan churning '' or " equity stripping, '' involves approving a borrower for a higher loan amount than they can reasonably afford, often with little regard for the borrower 's debt-to-income ( DTI ) ratio. This has resulted in a mortgage payment that is nearly half of my monthly salary, which is unsustainable and places me at high risk of financial distress and default. 

5. Negligent and Dismissive Behavior by Rocket Mortgage Executives When I contacted Rocket Mortgage 's executive team with my concerns, I was met with dismissive and shaming behavior. Despite multiple recorded calls in which I sought clarification and education on the mortgage terms, I was essentially told that it was my fault for not understanding the complexities of the mortgage contract ( see call with XXXX XXXX who also sighed at me ). This treatment, combined with the negligent approval of a loan amount that exceeds a reasonable DTI ratio, has left me in a precarious financial situation. 

6. Legal Grounds for Rescission The practices described above constitute fraudulent misrepresentation, deceptive trade practices, and a violation of consumer protection laws. Under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureaus regulations, I am entitled to rescind the mortgage contract due to the fraudulent origination practices employed by Rocket Mortgage. There is no statute of limitations when it comes to fraudulent activity. Furthermore, the reckless disregard for my ability to repay the loan, as evidenced by the inflated loan approval and disregard for my DTI ratio, and blatant conflicts of interests strengthens the legal grounds for rescission. 

Request for Amicable Resolution In light of these serious issues, I am requesting that Rocket Mortgage rescind my mortgage contract without penalty and return my down payment and closing cost, as well as the costs I incurred in lieu of this fraud. Violations include : Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), Fair Housing Act, Breach of Contract, violations to adhere of FHA guidelines and negligence.
